name: regression-or-group-primary-language
jd_fixture: synthetic, modelled on the ZoomInfo Senior SWE posting in #68
description: A backend crawling-infrastructure role whose must-have qualifications read 'Proficiency in Go and/or TypeScript' and whose 'Core Technical Stack' section restates both bare. The persona holds a TypeScript-primary hard gate and is a Go expert, so the posting is one they could take on their strongest language -- and the gate must not fire on the alternative they would never use. This is the ZoomInfo posting from #68 with the language pair swapped to the pair this profile actually gates on, so the case exercises the defect rather than merely resembling it.
comment: The enforced regression for #68. prefFieldsFor used to route prominence-claiming labels at required_skills and split OR-groups back apart, so any posting naming a gated technology tripped the gate: the live profile scored the original of this JD at 21.5 with the Python gate hit, and the narrative asserted the role 'gates on expert Python as a primary requirement' -- wording supplied by the preference label, never by the posting. Two mechanisms are under test here and both have to hold. (1) primary_stack is not alt-split, so 'Go | TypeScript' does not reach the TypeScript gate. (2) primary_stack ALSO restates 'TypeScript' and 'Go' bare alongside the group, mirroring the real posting's duplicate stack listing; collapseSubsumed is what makes that harmless. Re-add splitting, or drop the collapse, and this case fails.

screening_summary.industry: B2B web data and business intelligence
other_flags: anti-bot and proxy evasion is a named part of the work

gate_hits.comment: The posting offers Go as a substitute for TypeScript, and the persona is a Go expert. Nothing here is a gate.

preference_score.comment: Floor set above hardGateCeiling on purpose. A spurious gate hit caps at 25, so any score above it proves no gate fired -- which is the regression, not the exact arithmetic.

preference_conflicts.comment: distributed systems is a genuine match here, not a conflict; the point is that the prominence-claiming label does not appear.
must_exclude: TypeScript / Node.js as a primary language

preference_gaps.comment: #53. Both were structurally unearnable before the domain branch read core_competencies -- reported as gaps on a posting that requires distributed systems design outright.
